description:
## Goal

Make the compiler2 type interner's identity match the set-theoretic type
language:

    a and b are mutually subtype  iff  a == b

Every denotational type must have exactly one `Ty` in a `Types` arena. Keys
that embed `Ty` — especially `ActivationKey`, `ExecutableKey`, and `FactKey`
variants containing them — must therefore be canonical by construction.

## Current proof at origin/main a3a9761d1209165e5230625b9347cf6b0ad09b83

The defect remains live.

The committed regression
`canon_is_faithful_over_the_full_arena_of_both_target_fixtures` still counts
canonical-form collapses and asserts `collapsed > 0`, with an instruction to
change the expectation to zero when this ticket lands.

A disposable census using that test's existing `drive_fixture` path measured:

- `fixtures2/00420_enum_take_drop_split.fz`:
  1,166 arena IDs, 956 canonical forms, 210 excess equivalent IDs in 129
  duplicate classes.
- `fixtures2/behavior/fz_f98_range_map_converges.fz`:
  371 arena IDs, 322 canonical forms, 49 excess equivalent IDs in 18 duplicate
  classes.

A product-path census proves the duplication reaches real identity-bearing
work rather than remaining incidental arena debris:

- `00420`: 204 product activations contain 11 `(root, function, canonical
  arrow)` groups with two raw arrow IDs each.
- range-map: 59 product activations contain 4 such groups.

Examples include:

- `Enum.reverse_list/1`: arrow IDs 267 and 278 both denote
  `(list(int)) -> r0`.
- `Enum.reduce/3`: distinct arrow IDs denote
  `(list(int), empty_list(), closure[Enum.reverse/1#lambda…]()) -> r0`.
- The arena separately interns `[int]`, `[int] & not([])`, and their union even
  though all denote `non_empty_list(int)`.
- The arena separately interns `[]` and `[none]`, though both denote
  `empty_list()`.

`ActivationKey` derives `Eq` and `Hash` over its raw `arrow: Ty`, so these
pairs split activation, executable, and fact identity. Its current comment
that the arrow is canonical is false while this defect remains.

There is no current `SpecKey`; do not retain that stale name in the scope.

## Why the current persistence boundary is insufficient

`Types::intern` currently:

1. orders clauses,
2. drops provably-empty and pairwise-subsumed tuple clauses,
3. exact-deduplicates list, resource, function, and map clauses,
4. hashes the remaining `Descr`.

Those rules solve arrival order, exact `A | A`, and local tuple absorption.
They do not canonicalize semantically equal decompositions.

The stronger, faithful semantics already exist on the comparison-only side in
`compiler2/types/canon.rs`, including:

- whole-type and per-axis saturation,
- empty-clause removal on every structural axis,
- denotational list normalization,
- tuple coordinate widening for union-level redundancy,
- post-widening/subsumption removal,
- callable-literal identity independent of non-identifying arrow metadata.

That implementation renders external text and can construct temporary
descriptors; it is evidence for the required semantics, not itself a suitable
interner key.

## Strategy

Build one structural, idempotent normal-form pipeline at the type persistence
boundary.

- Define the normal form in descriptor/type data, not canonical-rendered
  strings and not an all-arena equivalence scan.
- Normalize child types bottom-up so every persisted descriptor references
  canonical child IDs.
- Preserve the existing stable clause ordering and exact-deduplication rules.
- Add the missing denotational rules proven by `TyCanon`: saturation,
  all-axis emptiness/subsumption, list normalization, and tuple-coordinate
  widening.
- Make tuple widening produce canonical interned child types through an
  explicit bottom-up DAG/build step; do not leave renderer-only temporary
  descriptors as a second identity language.
- Audit callable literals carefully. Their arrow surface is currently treated
  as metadata rather than value identity by subtyping/canonical rendering.
  If any consumer needs that metadata, move it to an explicit evidence
  structure instead of preserving multiple `Ty` identities for one value.
- Keep comparison-cache correctness obvious: aliases must never be minted, so
  no cache translation or lazy raw-ID equivalence table is required.
- Remove comparison-only normalization that becomes redundant, or document
  precisely why a remaining step is external-rendering work rather than type
  identity work.
- Update comments that currently claim `ActivationKey::arrow` is canonical only
  after the invariant is true.

Instrument normalization during development so the hot-path cost and rule hit
counts are visible on both target fixtures. Remove temporary instrumentation
before landing.

## TDD

Start red with focused identity tests that use `assert_eq!(left, right)`, not
only `is_equivalent`:

- `non_empty_list(T)` equals `list(T) & not([])`.
- `empty_list()` equals `list(none)`.
- The ticket's differently carved tuple unions intern to one ID.
- A saturated callable axis such as `(X) -> any` interns to the callable top
  independently of `X`.
- Equivalent closure-literal types cannot differ solely because of
  non-identifying surface metadata.
- Both construction/union orders reach the same exact ID.

Extend the full-arena ratchet so, for both target fixtures, no two distinct
arena slots are mutually subtype. Change the existing `collapsed > 0`
expectation to `collapsed == 0`; retain the canon faithfulness checks.

Add a product-path regression that groups activations by
`(root, function, canonical arrow)` and asserts that each group contains one
raw `ActivationKey.arrow`. This directly prevents the 11 + 4 currently
measured key splits.

## Acceptance

- Every `Ty` in each target fixture's full arena is unique modulo mutual
  subtyping.
- The committed canon faithfulness ratchet expects zero collapsed IDs.
- Product activation inventories contain no equivalent activation keys with
  different raw arrow IDs.
- `Types::intern` is idempotent and independent of construction/union order.
- Existing tuple absorption, exact-deduplication, activation-key ordering,
  canonical-form, and backend determinism tests remain green.
- No string-rendered type is used as the in-memory interner key.
- No lazy alias/translation table or full-arena scan is introduced.
- Temporary probes and counters are removed.
- Update `.agent/docs/set-theoretic-types.md` and
  `.agent/docs/canonical-form.md` to state the one-denotation/one-identity
  invariant and distinguish persistence normalization from external rendering.
- Run focused type/canon/product tests, `cargo test --lib`,
  the single-threaded fixture matrix, and clippy with warnings denied.

comments.text: DUPLICATE FOLDED (2026-09-03): fz-kdt.182 filed the same defect from the fz-kdt.120 research -- Types::union(empty_list(), list(int)) interns as `[] | [int]` though is_subtype(empty, list_int) holds (identical=false, is_equivalent=true, mutual subtypes), and fz-kdt.120's rule makes it visible (reduce at a ground reducer answers Known { result: [] | [int] }). Measured downstream at 0889c0b3a: activation keys carrying a `[] | [T]` union across the corpus: 1 at base (main/0#lambda@476-519/2[{any, any}, [] | [{any, any}]]), 0 under 120's prototype; render-identical duplicate executable keys 67 -> 40. So 120 does not need this first, but this ticket's "mutually-subtype types intern to one ID" is the general cure. 182 closed.

title: Make Ty identity denotational: mutually-subtype types intern to one ID
